title: Pull, don't push
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Tuesday. Day two. The mat cutter. The owner's hands over his on the blade. 'Pull, don't push.' The first straight cut of eleven years.

panels.composition: The frame shop. The mat cutter. WOOD at it, pushing the blade. The OWNER behind him, watching the cut wander.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a young man at a mat cutter pushing a blade along a rail while an older woman with glasses on a cord watches the cut wander

panels.composition: Her hands over his. Repositioning. The blade turned.

balloons.text: Pull. Don't push. The blade knows the way home; you don't.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, close-up of an older woman's hands placed over a young man's hands on a mat cutter's blade, turning it

panels.composition: The cut. Straight. A bevel like a shoreline.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, close-up of a clean straight bevel cut in white mat board

panels.composition: Wood holding it up to the window. The owner already back at her station. Not looking. Approving.

characters.pose: holding the mat to the light

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a young man holding a cut mat up to a window while an older woman works at her station without looking

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Pull, don't push.' 'Do four thousand.' (See dw_2018-02-09: he passes it on.)
